INSTALL_MASK: index patterns anchored with leading slash (bug 675826) For scalability, use a tree structure to index patterns that are anchored with a leading slash. CRAS: dev_io - Add the overrun op threshold On grunt, the number of frames an input node reads once is decided by a period size, whose default vaule is 1024. According to the latest overrun ops, if the device's hw_level is larger than 2 * largest_cb_level, the audio thread will drop frames. However, the cb_level of capture streams are 256 from ARC++ and 480 from Chrome. Both of them * 2 are less than 1024, it causes the overrun ops will be triggered every time. To fix the problem, we can add the overrun op threshold. The op only works when the hw_level is larger than that threshold. That time must to be longer than 2048 frames with rate 48000 (grunt only supports 48000 rate). Therefore, we think 50ms is a reasonable threshold. For users, it means that the delay will be reduced only if it is larger than 50ms. The value is too small to affect the user experience. Notice that we can not fix the problem by changing a period size on grunt because it will change a buffer size, too. (Buffer size = 2 * period size on grunt. See #22 on b/112860209) BUG=b:138076270, chromium:918462 TEST=The capture frames is not dropped on grunt and the delay keeps in 50ms on panther. Change-Id: Ibe367a2075fb6a49b45cca1449c895321c824585 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1708817 Tested-by: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Cheng-Yi Chiang <cychiang@chromium.org>

Increase timeout when fingers leave Sometimes when scrolling or swiping with multiple fingers, one finger will leave the edge of the touchpad before the others, causing the gesture with fewer fingers to be detected. This CL increases the timeout after an actively gesturing finger leaves before another gesture can be detected. It also now only suspends gesture detection when it is an actively gesturing finger that leaves. If a non-gesturing thumb or palm leaves the touchpad, gesture detection is not delayed. Remove close distance check for swipes With bigger touchpads on newer devices, people tend to spread their fingers out further when performing three or four finger swipes. As a result, the distance check to make sure all the fingers are close together has caused some missed gestures - three finger swipes that look like 2 finger scrolls or four finger swipes that look like three finger swipes. The distance check adds little value in filtering out palms for swipes, because swipes already require the fingers to be moving a significant distance in the same direction. This CL removes the distance check for three and four finger swipes entirely. xkeyboard-config: drop brokenbar from Swiss (German) layout Historically, the Swiss (German) layout has had two vertical bar characters: * Senkrechter Strich (U+007C, vertical line) * Unterbrochener Strich (U+00A6, broken bar) The broken bar is a relic from old school mechanical typesetting to have a character that looked different from uppercase-I and lowercase-l. Nowadays, the character does not have use for a typical user and only serves as a point of confusion when shells treat it differently from the regular vertical bar. For what it's worth, upstream xkeyboard-config and Mac OS X do not have this character in their layout. Windows appears to still have the character (at least in Windows 7). In the interest of reducing the number of Chrome OS specific patches to xkeyboard-config and reducing user confusion, we should drop this patch. Thanks to ricop@ on eng-misc for helping explain the historical context of this character.
